column3: Its casting from afar supplies a direct, though inverted, projectile counterpart to the focus's all-sided pelting.
Fear of territorial seizure is a remote boundary image and adds little to barred celestial audition.
The denunciation of a slanderer does not clarify the guarded assembly or its excluded listener.
It names the exalted assembly itself and frames it as a domain of knowledge not possessed by the speaker.
The opening ranks establish the ordered celestial force that the focus presents as controlling access.
Its call to hear and obey concerns testimony procedure, not restricted access to a protected source.
A setting without idle or false speech offers a secondary counterpart to the focus's regulated hearing field.
Immediate continuation specifies the stolen hearing and the piercing flame that pursues the intruder.
Hearing that receives a sign and yields response contrasts constructively with forbidden listening.
It distinguishes claiming to hear from actual receptive hearing, sharpening the focus's hearing boundary.
Its guarded sky against every expelled devil closely parallels the focus's defended upper enclosure.
The argument against multiple gods does not add to the focus's access-control scene.
Its protected speech environment repeats the auditory contrast already supplied by 78:35.

The highest horizon supplies a remote spatial echo without an access or defense relation.

Divine hearing and sight add only a generic observation motif.
The highest likeness is a theological comparison, not a celestial hearing boundary.

Covert visual tracking is only a distant analogy to prohibited listening.

Divine hearing in support of messengers is a broad constructive contrast.
Sealed hearts that do not hear provide an internal-obstruction counterpart to excluded audition.
Lordship over the heavens and their intervals reinforces the authority behind the guarded boundary.

Moses being brought near for private speech supplies a contrasting model of authorized access.

Casting through water is lexical overlap only and does not illuminate celestial exclusion.
The elite's accusation of error is unrelated to controlled hearing above.

Safe hearing of God's speech offers a terrestrial contrast in which access is deliberately granted.
The comprehensive punishment statement does not specify hearing or the guarded enclosure.
Casting truth from the knower of the unseen gives a secondary projectile parallel to the focus.
The court's magic label before an elite is not a meaningful counterpart to the exalted assembly.
Return to God and divine power do not clarify the scene of excluded listening.
The single rebuke followed by compelled seeing extends the passage's decisive commanding force.
Hearing a revealed book and recognizing its guidance supplies a constructive counterpart to illicit audition.
The Mount-side appointment and provision do not clarify the focus's guarded hearing.
Its later truth-and-messengers assertion is too distant from the focus's access scene.
Divine hearing and knowledge are a broad attribute parallel only.
The side-directed punishment image is too remote despite its downward and upward hazards.
Casting terror into hearts offers a secondary casting image of defenses being overcome.
Divine provision and knowledge do not illuminate barred access to the exalted assembly.
The return and recompense scene adds no specific hearing or enclosure relation.
The later blessing on Moses and Aaron does not clarify the focus passage.
The question whether objects can hear calls isolates reception capacity, a relevant contrast to forbidden hearing.
Its human elite and battle commitment do not add to celestial access control.
The later blessing on Elias does not clarify the guarded-sky sequence.
Treating unheard teaching as fabrication gives a social counterpart to a closed hearing horizon.
The fire seen at the Mount's side has no specific access or hearing relation.
Truth's arrival and falsehood's collapse repeat the projectile-truth strand already covered.
Seeking the face of the highest Lord does not clarify the exalted assembly.
The universal messenger pattern does not add to the specific guarded-listening scene.
The later rescue statement is unrelated to the focus passage.
Hearing within divorce procedure does not clarify celestial audition.
Repentance and its reward do not add to the focus's access-control reading.
The piercing star closely echoes the penetrating flame that follows the eavesdropper.
Divine listening alongside the messengers supplies an authorized and protective contrast.
Casting ornaments is lexical overlap without the guarded-hearing relation.
The later denial-and-presence statement does not clarify the focus passage.
The courtly command to listen is a remote social parallel and adds little after stronger hearing cards.
Not hearing the sound of punishment is a distant protected-auditory contrast.
The guardian motif supports a broader image of vigilant protection around a bounded domain.
Witnessing and recompense do not clarify the focus's guarded listening.
The failure of an obstinate tyrant has no specific relation to the focus.
The later drink description does not add to the guarded-sky sequence.
The call to hear a believer is a general reception appeal, already well represented.
It explicitly states that the rival transmitters are isolated from hearing, directly paralleling exclusion.
The sky and night visitor retain the upper-boundary and piercing-light resonance.
Hearing a will and altering it is a legal setting unrelated to the focus.
Mixing and concealing truth gives a broad information-integrity contrast only.
The closing blessing on messengers does not clarify the focus passage.
The list of favored prophets has no guarded-hearing relation.
It makes hearing, sight, and inward judgment accountable, cautioning against unsupported pursuit of knowledge.
The same-surah claim of kinship with jinn and their accountability provides relevant surrounding context for the intruder class.
Listening to day-night signs is a broad constructive hearing motif only.
Listening for lies and distorting words supplies a corrupted-reception contrast to the guarded source.
Divine selection of angelic and human messengers supports controlled, authorized transmission.
Divine all-encompassing presence does not specify the exalted assembly's guarded boundary.
Thrown fragments of hearing and their prevalent falsehood clarify why illicit reception is not reliable transmission.
The debt-writing procedure does not illuminate the focus.
Rescue from distress and subsequent association do not clarify the guarded-hearing scene.
The burned-garden parable has no material relation to the focus.
The incapacity to hear or respond supplies a distinct reception-failure contrast.
Its communal inconsistency and punishment do not clarify the focus.
Hearing, sight, and hearts failing through denial gives a final broader contrast to meaningful reception.
It explicitly makes the lamps of the lowest heaven missiles against devils, supplying the focus's defensive celestial armament.
The jinn find the heaven filled with stern guards and flames, directly restating the guarded enclosure.
Former listening stations are now met by a waiting flame, making the prohibition and interception explicit.
The lowest heaven is adorned with lamps and made a guarded domain, a close structural parallel to 37:6-8.
The trustworthy Spirit's authorized descent provides the positive transmission counterpart to forbidden eavesdropping.
It expressly denies that the devils brought the revelation down, delimiting the source against illicit transmitters.
The devils are declared neither suited nor able to bring it, strengthening the exclusion of unauthorized access.
The question of whom devils descend upon introduces the false-transmission alternative completed by the adjacent hearing verses.
Their receipt of fragments of hearing directly explains the unreliable, illicit channel opposed to the focus.
The message is carried by a noble messenger, supplying an authorized celestial transmission line.
The messenger's strength gives a secondary contrast to the vulnerable intruder pursued in 37:10.
The trusted, obeyed messenger depicts legitimate access and authority within the celestial order.
It rejects attribution of the message to an expelled devil, directly reinforcing the focus's exclusion premise.
The knower of the unseen does not disclose it indiscriminately, framing hidden knowledge as controlled access.
Guards sent before and behind an approved messenger provide an explicit protection model for disclosed knowledge.
The protected ceiling image gives a broader structural counterpart to the guarded heaven.
The honored servants' status supplies a positive counterpart to rebellious beings excluded from the upper order.
They do not precede the divine word and act only by command, clarifying regulated celestial communication.
The imagined opening into heaven and ascent supplies an adjacent boundary-crossing counterpart to the focus.
Jinn listening attentively to recitation provides a deliberate, terrestrial contrast to prohibited celestial listening.
Jinn hearing the Quran and responding favorably further distinguishes received revelation from stolen hearing.
The jinn's failure to know the unseen limits their claimed access to hidden celestial knowledge.
Gabriel's descent by divine permission gives an authorized revelation route against unauthorized interception.
The Holy Spirit's truthful descent supplies another explicit authorized-transmission counterpart.
The angels and Spirit descend only by their Lord's permission, emphasizing regulated heavenly movement.
The command expelling Iblis provides background for the hostile class barred from the protected heaven.
Iblis is identified as jinn who rebelled against his Lord, linking jinn rebellion to exclusion from divine order.
Human and jinn devils exchange embellished speech, a terrestrial false-message contrast to guarded celestial hearing.
Satan's attempted insertion into recitation supplies a contrasting interference model that divine action removes.
